riot.title: Notice required by Riot Games
riot.intro: Riot Games requires every third-party product to display the following notice in a place that is readily visible to players. It is reproduced word for word, in its official English wording.
riot.text: {{product}} isn't endorsed by Riot Games and doesn't reflect the views or opinions of Riot Games or anyone officially involved in producing or managing Riot Games properties. Riot Games, and all associated properties are trademarks or registered trademarks of Riot Games, Inc.

meta.title: Terms of use — {{product}}
meta.description: {{product}}'s terms of use: purpose of the service, sign-in through Discord, League of Legends account, published content, availability and intellectual property.

hero.title: Terms of use
hero.subtitle: What each side commits to when using {{product}}.

purpose.title: Purpose
purpose.p1: Schub is a personal, free and non-commercial project hosted on schultz-thomas.fr. It gathers the tools of the Miam Discord community: today, control over game servers hosted at home and support for a League of Legends team — roster, statistics, champion pool, composition planning and post-game review.
purpose.p2: Using the site means accepting these terms. Anyone who does not accept them simply does not create an account; server status and the text pages remain readable without one.
purpose.p1_PremadeLab: PremadeLab is a personal, free and non-commercial project hosted on premadelab.eu. It is a League of Legends game analysis tool, for a player and for their team: player search, statistics and findings on their games, roster, champion pool, composition planning and post-game review.
purpose.p2_PremadeLab: Using the site means accepting these terms. Anyone who does not accept them simply does not create an account; the presentation, player pages and text pages remain readable without one.

publisher.title: Publisher
publisher.p1: The site is published and hosted privately and non-professionally by Thomas Schultz, a private individual living in Colmar (France). His full postal address is provided on request, through the contact form.
publisher.p2: No email address is published on this site: the contact form is the open channel, and it is also the one used for any request concerning data.

account.title: Account and access
account.p1: Sign-in goes through Discord. A Discord account is therefore required, along with compliance with Discord's own terms, over which the publisher has no control. No password is created or kept for {{product}}.
account.p2: An account's rights follow a role granted by the publisher. A newly created account only reaches its own profile and its own statistics; access to teams and to administration is granted case by case.
account.p3: The publisher may suspend or close an access, without notice, in case of abuse — in particular declaring a game account that does not belong to the person, or writing the content listed below.

riotAccount.title: League of Legends account
riotAccount.p1: Declaring a Riot ID triggers the reading of that account's public history through the Riot Games API. Declare only your own account: declaring someone else's amounts to having their games collected without their consent.
riotAccount.p2: A declared account is not unlinked, it is replaced. Replacing it resets personal statistics and restarts a collection; the consequences are shown and require confirmation before being applied.
riotAccount.p3: {{product}} does not interact with the game client, changes nothing in the game and provides no in-game advantage. It only reads data that the Riot Games API exposes publicly.

content.title: What you publish
content.p1: Team names, compositions, their notes and post-game reviews are written by users. They are visible to the members of the team concerned, and to no one else.
content.p2: You remain responsible for what you write. The following are excluded, and removed without notice:
content.i1: insults, harassment and discriminatory statements, including those aimed at a teammate named in a review;
content.i2: third parties' personal data — address, phone number, civil identity — which has no place in a game note;
content.i3: any unlawful content, or content infringing a third party's rights.
content.p3: A post-game review is about a game: it describes play, not a person.

availability.title: Availability and warranties
availability.p1: The service is provided as is, free of charge, with no warranty whatsoever as to availability, accuracy or preservation. It runs on a personal machine: a power cut, a hardware failure or a move stops it.
availability.p2: The publisher may change, restrict or shut down the service, in whole or in part, without notice and without compensation. The statistics shown are computed from game data: they may be incomplete or wrong, and they ground no decision binding anyone.
availability.p3: To the fullest extent permitted by law, the publisher cannot be held liable for any damage, direct or indirect, arising from the use of the service, its unavailability or the loss of the data it holds. Nothing in these terms excludes a liability that the law does not allow to be excluded.

ip.title: Intellectual property
ip.p1: League of Legends, champion names and artwork, the icons served by Data Dragon and all game assets belong to Riot Games, Inc. {{product}} uses them as a third-party product, under the rules of the Riot Games developer portal.
ip.p2: {{product}}'s code is published under the licence of its public repository. Content written by users — team names, compositions, reviews — remains theirs; the publisher only uses it to operate the service.

privacy.title: Personal data
privacy.p1: What is collected, where it lives, for how long and how to ask for its deletion is described in the privacy policy.

changes.title: Changes to these terms
changes.p1: These terms may change, in particular if the service changes. The date of the last update appears at the top of the page. Continuing to use the site after a change means accepting the version in force.

law.title: Governing law
law.p1: These terms are governed by French law. Failing an amicable settlement, any dispute falls under the competent French courts. A user acting as a consumer keeps the protection of the mandatory rules of their country of residence.

meta.title: Privacy policy — {{product}}
meta.description: What {{product}} collects — Discord identity, Riot ID, public match history, review notes —, where that data lives, for how long, and how to ask for its deletion.

hero.title: Privacy policy
hero.subtitle: What is collected, why, where it lives, for how long, and how to have it erased.

controller.title: Who processes this data
controller.p1: Data is processed by Thomas Schultz, publisher of the site, a private individual living in Colmar (France), privately and non-commercially. His full postal address is provided on request.
controller.p2: No email address is published: every request goes through the site's contact form.

collected.title: What is collected
collected.discord: On sign-in, Discord provides the account identifier, its username and its avatar address. Nothing else: no Discord email address, no server list, no messages.
collected.account: The display name chosen on the site, the role granted and the permissions that follow from it, the creation date and the last sign-in date.
collected.riot: The declared Riot ID (name and tag) and the puuid Riot associates with it. The puuid is never returned to the browser: it stays server-side, because a Riot identifier handed to the client is the key to probing someone's history.
collected.matches: For every game read through the Riot Games API, Riot's response is kept as is, and a per-player projection is derived from it: champion, position, queue, result, side, duration, patch, kills, deaths, assists, minions, gold, damage to champions, vision score, whether the player went absent, and date. Current rankings and champion masteries are added to that.
collected.othersTitle: The other players in those games
collected.others: A game holds ten participants. The Riot ID and game figures of the other nine are therefore recorded too, including when they have no {{product}} account and never will. That data is made public by the Riot Games API, but it is indeed kept here — and a deletion request covers it as well.
collected.teams: A team's name, its roster — a Riot ID, positions and a status per seat —, the champion pool it keeps per position and the compositions prepared, with their patch and notes.
collected.reviews: The free-form text written by one member about another, attached to a specific game, with its author, its subject and its creation and edit dates.
collected.contact: The name, email address and message entered. The site does not store them: the message is delivered as is to the publisher through Discord, as a direct message or in a fallback channel, and stays in that messaging service until the publisher deletes it.

notCollected.title: What is not collected
notCollected.i1: no password: sign-in goes through Discord;
notCollected.i2: no advertising tracker, no ad network, no commercial profiling;
notCollected.i3: no third-party analytics. The only audience measure is a daily count of the distinct people who use player search: no cookie, based on a hash of the IP address and browser salted every day, which identifies no one and is erased after 31 days;
notCollected.i4: no payment data: the service is free and bills nothing.

cookies.title: Cookies and browser storage
cookies.session: A session cookie, set by the server and unreachable from the site's JavaScript, carries the authentication token. It is required to operate: without it there is no sign-in. Signing out erases it.
cookies.local: The browser keeps one setting locally, under the key color-mode: the choice between light and dark theme. It never leaves the device.
cookies.turnstile: The contact form may be protected by Cloudflare Turnstile, an anti-bot service. When it is enabled, the browser contacts Cloudflare, which then sees the visitor's IP address and applies its own policy. With no key configured, the widget is not loaded at all.

purposes.title: Why this data is processed
purposes.i1: to identify a person and grant the rights attached to their role;
purposes.i2: to attach a game account to a site account, and to a roster seat;
purposes.i3: to compute and display personal and team statistics;
purposes.i4: to operate teams: roster, champion pool, compositions, reviews;
purposes.i5: to receive contact form messages and keep spam out.
purposes.basis: Legal basis: performance of the service you request by creating an account (GDPR, Article 6(1)(b)) for your account, your teams and your content; legitimate interest (Article 6(1)(f)) for other players’ game data, which the Riot Games API makes public and without which no statistic exists, as well as for the contact form and its protection against spam.

storage.title: Where this data lives
storage.p1: In a self-hosted MongoDB database, on the machine that hosts the site. No data is handed to a third-party database host, an analytics service or an online backup service.
storage.p2: This machine is located in France, at the publisher’s home. There is no backup outside this machine: a failure can lose data, as the terms of use say.

retention.title: For how long
retention.caches: Rankings, champion masteries and the game version are fetched again after a few hours. These are caches: they are replaced, not accumulated.
retention.permanent: Collected games, their per-player projections and the index of game accounts encountered have no expiry date.
retention.riotPurge: This has to be said plainly: {{product}} only collects each player's recent games, and Riot itself only serves a capped history. The games already collected, however, stay. In other words, {{product}} keeps games that Riot no longer serves, and that is what makes a deletion request meaningful.
retention.account: The account, its teams, its compositions and its reviews are kept as long as the account exists. Deleting a team deletes its compositions and its reviews.

sharing.title: Who this data is shared with
sharing.p1: No one. Nothing is sold, rented, transferred or passed to a third party for commercial, advertising or statistical purposes.
sharing.p2: Three outside services are nonetheless involved, and it is fair to name them:
sharing.i1: Riot Games — the site queries its API to read games. What leaves here is the identifier of the game account concerned, nothing more;
sharing.i2: Discord — for authentication, and for delivering contact form messages;
sharing.i3: Cloudflare — only if the contact form's anti-bot protection is enabled.
sharing.p3: Data also stays visible to those who need it on the site: a team's members see that team's roster, statistics and reviews. A player's public page shows any visitor what the Riot Games API makes public: their Riot ID, rank, champions and game statistics. Team notes, compositions and reviews are never public.

rights.title: What you can ask for
rights.p1: To see what concerns you, to have it corrected, to have it erased, or to object to its collection.
rights.selfTitle: What you can do yourself, today
rights.self1: change your display name, from your profile;
rights.self2: replace your declared game account — personal statistics then start over from zero;
rights.self4: delete a team you created, or remove a member from it.
rights.gap: There is no account deletion button, and it would be dishonest to suggest otherwise. Deleting an account and the game data attached to it is done by hand, on request.
rights.how: Through the site’s contact form, stating the Discord username or the Riot ID concerned. The publisher undertakes to reply within one month and to confirm what was erased. You can also lodge a complaint with the CNIL, the French data protection authority (cnil.fr).
rights.thirdParty: This channel is open to people with no {{product}} account too: if your Riot ID appears here because you crossed paths with a user in a game, the same request applies, through the same form.

minors.title: Minors
minors.p1: The site is not aimed at children and asks for no age, because it could not verify it. Access requires a Discord account, and therefore the minimum age Discord sets in the user’s country.

changes.title: Changes
changes.p1: This policy follows the code: it changes when the service changes. The date of the last update appears at the top of the page.
